summary: Active in Tibetology and linguistics, Jampa Lhundup studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, where he is attested as Assistant Professor of Art History and faculty member in 2026.

Jampa Losang Panglung (1939–2022) specialized in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned a Geshe Lharamapa at Sera Monastery and completed his Magister and doctorate at the University of Munich, later serving in dictionary and research roles at the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities.
Working in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Jampa Mackenzie Stewart studied under traditional teachers Khenpo Karthar Rinpoche and Jamgon Kongtrul Lodro Chokyi Senge.

Specializing in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Jampa Samten served as a bibliographer at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives (attested 1987). At the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, he served as Director (attested 2003–2004) and Professor (attested 2015, 2026).
Jampal Kunzang Rechung (b. 1930) worked in Tibetology. He served as Deputy Director at the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology (attested 1982) and edited the Bulletin of Tibetology (attested 1980–1988).

Jamphel Yeshe Gyaltsen (1912–1947) worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under the 13th Dalai Lama, Kalu Rinpoche, Chatral Sangye Dorje, and Tsennyi Tulku Jampal Norbu, and taught the 14th Dalai Lama and 19th Kushok Bakula Rinpoche.

Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö (1893–1959) was an active figure in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under numerous teachers, including Khenpo Thupten, Shechen Gyaltsab, and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, and succeeded Dzongsar Khyentse Jamyang Chökyi Wangpo.

Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo (1820–1892) was a master in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under numerous teachers, including Rigdzin Zangpo and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, and taught figures such as Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso.
Jamyang Sherab Chokyi Nangwa studied under Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye.
Jan A. Schoterman (1948–1989) was an Indologist. He studied under Jan Gonda and completed a doctoral thesis at Utrecht University under supervisor Henk Bodewitz (attested 1982).

Jan Chozen Bays (b. 1945) works in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied at Swarthmore College and UC San Diego, trained under Taizan Maezumi and Shodo Harada, and served as abbess at Great Vow Zen Monastery around 2002.
Working in Indology and computational studies, Jan Christian Schaffert studied as a Bearbeiter and worked on the EdiKILex project at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2026).
Specializing in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Jan Dolensky earned a Magister der Philosophie at the University of Vienna under the supervision of Klaus-Dieter Mathes (attested 2013).

Jan E. M. Houben specializes in Indology, linguistics, and philosophy. He held posts at the Dutch Research Council (attested 1999), Leiden University (attested 2000–2002), and the École Pratique des Hautes Études as a directeur d’études (attested 2009–2012).

Jan Fontein (1927–2017) specialized in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He completed his PhD at Leiden University under Theodoor Paul Galestin, and held curatorial posts at the Rijksmuseum and the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston (1966–1992).

Jan Gonda (1905–1991) worked in Indology, linguistics, and religious studies. He studied at Utrecht University (PhD) and Leiden University, and served at Utrecht University as Chair of Sanskrit (1929) and Professor of Indology (1932–1976).

Jan Jakob Maria de Groot (1854–1921) specialized in Sinology and religious studies. He studied at Leiden University and under Georg von der Gabelentz, later serving as professor at Leiden University (1891–1912) and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1912–1921).
Jan Jaworski (1903–1945) was a scholar in Sinology, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Warsaw (~1921–1927) and trained under Stanisław Schayer and Jean Przyluski.

Jan Julius Lodewijk Duyvendak (1889–1954) was a Sinologist who studied at Leiden University, the Sorbonne, and Humboldt University of Berlin. He held visiting professorships at Columbia, Princeton, and Oxford, and served as Professor of Chinese at Leiden University (1930–1954).

Jan N. Bremmer (b. 1944) works in religious studies and history/archaeology. He completed PhDs at VU Amsterdam and the University of Amsterdam, served as Assistant Professor at Utrecht University (1974–1990), and held the Chair of Religious Studies at Groningen (1990).
